newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees tourism surplus surge cutting C/A gap.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees tourism surplus surge cutting C/A gap.

text.p: Hungary is likely to double the surplus of its balance of payment in tourism in 1996, improving the current account considerably, the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) said on Monday, quoted by the Hungarian news agency MTI.

The surplus would probably amount to some $1.3 billion this year, up from $659 million last year, the NBH said, adding that revenues from tourism were likely to rise to above $2.2 billion in 1996 from $1.71 billion in 1995, the central bank added.
Tourism is one of the main components of the current account.

Hungary originally targeted to reduce its current account deficit to $2 billion this year from $2.5 billion in 1995, but finance ministry and central bank officials said recently that the 1996 deficit may be as low as $1.5 billion.
The current account deficit was $1.12 billion in October.
